<header>諸品經第二十八卷上 / ᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪ (eldeb)</header>
<meta>Peking Mongolian Kanjur woodblock print (xylograph) in vermilion ink, pothi format; 25 vertical lines of Classical Mongolian script read left-to-right, with a Mongolian marginal signature on the left and a Chinese marginal signature on the right.</meta>
<warning>Vermilion blockprint ink shows moderate fading and low contrast in the left margin and in several columns on the right side of the page.</warning>

<margin>ᠡᠯᠳᠡᠪ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠵᠠᠭᠤᠨ ᠶᠢᠡᠨ ᠭᠤᠷᠪᠠᠨ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ (eldeb gurban jagun yiren gurban deger-e)</margin>
<margin>諸品經第二十八卷上三百九十三</margin>

○ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠭᠡᠮ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ <term>ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ</term> ᠢ ᠄ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠ <unclear>ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡᠬᠦᠢ</unclear> ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄
ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠲᠤᠷ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠣᠭ ᠲᠤ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄
ᠭᠡᠮ ᠦᠳ ᠢ ᠲᠡᠪᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠲᠤᠷ ᠲᠡᠪᠴᠢᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ
ᠪᠤᠶᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠴᠢᠮᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠰᠠᠶᠢᠨ ᠴᠢᠮᠡᠭ ᠲᠦ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄
ᠰᠡᠳᠬᠢᠯ ᠢ ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠨᠣᠮᠣᠭᠠᠳᠬᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠨᠣᠮᠣᠭᠠᠨ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄
ᠲᠡᠳᠡᠭᠡᠷ ᠢ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠ ᠄ ᠲᠡᠶᠢᠨ ᠪᠦᠭᠡᠳ ᠢᠯᠠᠭᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄
ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠠᠮᠤᠷܠᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠠᠮᠤᠷܠᠢᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠣᠷᠣᠨ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄
ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠳᠤ ᠳᠤ ᠬᠦᠷᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠦ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠭᠡᠲᠦᠯᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄ ᠮᠠᠰᠢ
ᠲᠣᠨᠢᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠲᠣᠨᠢᠯᠭᠠᠭᠴᠢ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄ ᠮᠠᠰᠢ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰᠦᠭᠰᠡᠨ
 ᠦ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠢ ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠴᠢ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄ <term>ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ</term>
 ᠤ <term>ᠪᠡᠯᠭᠡ ᠪᠢᠯᠢᠭ</term> ᠲᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠢᠯᠡᠳᠲᠡ <term>ᠪᠤᠷᠬᠠᠨ</term> ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄
ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ <term>ᠨᠣᠮ</term> ᠤᠳ ᠢ ᠠᠶᠢᠯᠠᠳᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠨᠢᠳᠦ ᠲᠦ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄
ᠮᠡᠳᠡᠭᠳᠡᠬᠦᠢ ᠶᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠦᠯᠦᠭᠴᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠢ ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠴᠢ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ
ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠳᠡᠭᠡᠳᠦ ᠪᠣᠯᠤᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠡᠷᠬᠡᠲᠦ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ
ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠄ ᠲᠡᠭᠦᠰ ᠪᠦᠷᠢᠨ ᠦᠭᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠠᠷᠢᠭᠤᠨ ᠦᠭᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠨᠡᠷ᠎ᠡ ᠲᠦ ᠪᠤᠶᠤ ᠅

ᠭᠤᠴᠢᠨ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠷ <term>ᠶᠡᠬᠡ ᠨᠢᠭᠦᠯᠡᠰᠬᠦᠢ</term> ᠠᠯᠢ ᠪᠤᠢ ᠬᠡᠮᠡᠪᠡᠰᠦ ᠄ ᠀
ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ <term>ᠨᠣᠮ</term> ᠤᠳ ᠢ ᠪᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠠᠮᠢᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄
ᠲᠡᠵᠢᠭᠡᠭᠴᠢ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ <term>ᠪᠣᠳᠭᠠᠯᠢ</term> ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠣᠷᠣᠰᠢᠬᠤ ᠄
ᠦᠯᠦ ᠲᠥᠷᠥᠬᠦ ᠄ ᠦᠯᠦ ᠭᠠᠷᠬᠤ ᠄ <unclear>ᠦᠯᠦ ᠠᠭᠤᠯᠵᠠᠬᠤ</unclear> ᠄ ᠪᠥᠭᠡᠳ ᠄
ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠦᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ <term>ᠪᠣᠳᠢᠰᠤᠭ</term> ᠤᠨ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠰ᠎ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ
ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ <term>ᠶᠡᠬᠡ ᠨᠢᠭᠦᠯᠡᠰᠬᠦᠢ</term> ᠶᠢ ᠡᠭᠦᠰᠬᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠄ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠠᠩᠬ᠎ᠠ <term>ᠶᠡᠬᠡ
ᠨᠢᠭᠦᠯᠡᠰᠬᠦᠢ</term> ᠪᠣᠯᠠᠢ ᠄ ᠪᠠᠰᠠ ᠬᠠᠮᠤᠭ <term>ᠨᠣᠮ</term> ᠤᠳ ᠢ ᠣᠷᠣᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄
<unclear>ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠯᠳᠤᠯᠭ᠎ᠠ</unclear> ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠬᠤ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠄ ᠥᠪᠡᠷ ᠦᠨ ᠴᠢᠨᠠᠷ ᠢᠶᠠᠷ
ᠠᠭᠰᠠᠨ ᠦᠭᠡᠢ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠᠳᠠ ᠄ ᠠᠮᠢᠲᠠᠨ ᠤ ᠲᠤᠰ᠎ᠠ ᠶᠢᠨ ᠲᠤᠯᠠ <term>ᠶᠡᠬᠡ ᠨᠢᠭᠦᠯᠡᠰᠬᠦᠢ</term>
 ᠶᠢ ᠡᠭᠦᠰᠬᠡᠭᠰᠡᠨ ᠄ ᠡᠨᠡ ᠪᠡᠷ ᠬᠣᠶᠠᠳᠤᠭᠠᠷ <term>ᠶᠡᠬᠡ ᠨᠢᠭᠦᠯᠡᠰᠬᠦᠢ</term> ᠪᠣᠯᠠᠢ ᠄

<note>Romanized transliteration (lines 1–25):

8. činadu-du kürügsen-ü tulada : getülügsen ner-e-tü buyu : maši
9. tonilugsan-u tulada : maši tonilgagči ner-e-tü buyu : maši tegüsügsen
10. -ü tulada : qamug-i medegči ner-e-tü buyu : burqan
11. -u belge bilig-tü bolugsan-u tulada : iledte burqan ner-e-tü buyu :
12. qamug nom-ud-i ayiladugsan-u tulada : nidü-tü ner-e-tü buyu :
13. medegdeküi-yi üjegülügči-yin tulada : qamug-i üjegči ner-e-tü

21. tulada yeke nigülesküi-yi egüskegsen : ene ber angq-a yeke
22. nigülesküi bolai : basa qamug nom-ud-i oron ügei :
23. barildulg-a ügei : bariqu ügei : öber-ün činar-iyar
24. agsan ügei-yin tulada : amitan-u tus-a-yin tula yeke nigülesküi
25. -yi egüskegsen : ene ber qoyadugar yeke nigülesküi bolai :</note>

<margin><term>Eldeb</term> <gloss>Miscellaneous Sūtras section</gloss>, three hundred ninety-three, upper <note>folio 393a, recto; original: "eldeb gurban jagun yiren gurban deger-e"</note></margin>
<margin>Sūtras of Various Sections, Scroll Twenty-Eight, Upper Part, Three Hundred Ninety-Three <note>original: "諸品經第二十八卷上三百九十三"</note></margin>

○ <note>Because one beholds</note> the transcendent and faultless <term>burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha, the Awakened One</gloss>, he is called <unclear>ᠦᠵᠡᠭᠳᠡᠬᠦᠢ</unclear> by All;
because he abides well, he is called Possessed of Noble Splendor <note>original: "sayin čog-tu"</note>;
because he has abandoned all faults, he is called the One Who Has Well Abandoned <note>original: "sayitur tebčigsen"</note>;
because he is adorned with the marks of merit, he is called the Finely Adorned One <note>original: "sayin čimeg-tü"</note>;
because he has thoroughly tamed his mind, he is called the Thoroughly Serene One <note>original: "maši nomogan", literally "thoroughly tamed" or "gentle"</note>;
because he has conquered those <note>afflictions and hostile forces</note>, he is called the Completely Victorious One <note>original: "teyin büged ilagugsan"</note>;
because he has become thoroughly peaceful, he is called the Abode of Supreme Peace <note>original: "maši amurligsan oron"</note>;
because he has reached the further shore, he is called the One Who Has Crossed Over <note>original: "getülügsen"</note>; because he is thoroughly
liberated, he is called the Supreme Liberator <note>original: "maši tonilgagči"</note>; because he is thoroughly perfected,
he is called the All-Knowing One <note>original: "qamug-i medegči"</note>; because he has come to possess the <term>burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha</gloss>
<term>belge bilig</term> <gloss>primordial wisdom or gnosis, Sanskrit jñāna</gloss>, he is called the Manifest <term>burqan</term> <gloss>Buddha, the Fully Awakened One</gloss>;
because he has realized all <term>nom</term> <gloss>phenomena or teachings, Sanskrit dharma</gloss>, he is called the One Possessed of the Eye <note>original: "nidü-tü"</note>;
because he reveals all that is knowable, he is called the All-Seeing One <note>original: "qamug-i üjegči"</note>;
because he has become the supreme one among all sentient beings, he is called the Sovereign Lord <note>original: "erketü", Sanskrit īśvara</note>;
and because he possesses perfect and complete speech, he is called the One of Pure Speech <note>original: "arigun üge-tü"</note>.

If one asks what the thirty-two <term>yeke nigülesküi</term> <gloss>great compassions, Sanskrit mahākaruṇā</gloss> are:
All <term>nom</term> <gloss>phenomena, Sanskrit dharma</gloss> are without self <note>original: "bi ügei", Sanskrit anātman</note>, without sentient being <note>original: "amitan ügei", Sanskrit niḥsattva</note>, without life-force <note>original: "amin ügei", Sanskrit nirjīva</note>,
without a sustainer <note>original: "tejigegči ügei", Sanskrit niṣpoṣa</note>, without a <term>bodgali</term> <gloss>individual person, Sanskrit pudgala</gloss>, non-abiding <note>original: "ülü orošiqu"</note>,
unborn <note>original: "ülü törökü", Sanskrit ajāta</note>, unarisen <note>original: "ülü garqu", Sanskrit anutpanna</note>, and <unclear>ᠦᠯᠦ ᠠᠭᠤᠯᠵᠠᠬᠤ</unclear>;
because they lack inherent nature <note>original: "öber-ün činar ügei", Sanskrit niḥsvabhāva</note>, the <term>bodisug</term> <gloss>bodhisattva, an awakening being</gloss>, for the benefit of sentient beings,
generates <term>yeke nigülesküi</term> <gloss>great compassion</gloss>; this is the first
<term>yeke nigülesküi</term> <gloss>great compassion</gloss>. Furthermore, because all <term>nom</term> <gloss>phenomena</gloss> are without abode <note>original: "oron ügei", Sanskrit asthāna</note>,
without <unclear>ᠪᠠᠷᠢᠯᠳᠤᠯᠭᠠ</unclear>, without grasping <note>original: "bariqu ügei", Sanskrit agrāhya</note>, and by their own nature
do not exist <note>original: "öber-ün činar-iyar agsan ügei"</note>, for the benefit of sentient beings he generates <term>yeke nigülesküi</term> <gloss>great compassion</gloss>;
this is the second <term>yeke nigülesküi</term> <gloss>great compassion</gloss>.

<note>This folio from the Miscellaneous Sūtras section, Classical Mongolian Eldeb, of the Peking Mongolian Kanjur concludes a canonical litany explaining the epithets of the Buddha through his spiritual realizations and virtues, and then introduces the doctrinal exposition of the thirty-two great compassions of a bodhisattva, grounding compassionate action in the emptiness and non-self of all phenomena.</note>

<summary>This folio from Volume 28 of the Miscellaneous Sūtras section of the Peking Mongolian Kanjur concludes a list of epithets of the Buddha paired with the spiritual qualities that justify each title. It then begins an exposition of the thirty-two great compassions of a bodhisattva, explaining how the first two arise from realizing that all phenomena lack a self, an individual person, or inherent existence.</summary>
